subject: Mutual action plan + TTFT streaming benchmark — proposed timeline
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Suresh Patel <suresh@medsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan + TTFT streaming benchmark — proposed timeline

Suresh —

Thanks again for the meeting this morning. Per our conversation I put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) focused on validating TTFT and streaming latencies for your chat assistant use case and closing before year-end. Attached is medsys_map_v1.pdf with the milestones. High level:

- Objective: Validate end-to-end TTFT (time-to-first-token) and streaming latency at target concurrency to confirm SLAs for launch.
- Scope: rwd-vicuna-13b (quantized) on Dedicated pool; evaluation against 3 prompt classes (short/medium/long) and 3 concurrency targets (1, 8, 32).
- Metrics we will report: TTFT p50/p95/p99, streaming per-token latency p50/p95/p99, sustained throughput (tokens/s) under steady-state, error rate (5xx / infrastructure errors).
- Proposed timeline:
  - Nov 23: Share evaluation harness and test prompts (we will provide the harness and seed prompts)
  - Nov 25: Redwood runs initial bench and shares raw CSV results + summary (we expect to run both cold-cache and warmed KV-cache scenarios)
  - Nov 29: Joint review and finalize canary window
  - Dec 7–9: Customer canary (small production traffic, Redwood support oncall)
  - Dec 14: Target full cutover / GA for the feature if canary meets KPIs

Deliverables we will attach on Nov 25: raw results (ttft_stream_results.csv), summarized p50/p95/p99 tables, and a short playbook for canary run (medsys_canary_playbook.docx).

Questions for you now so we can lock schedule:
1) Are the proposed concurrency targets (1/8/32) representative of the load patterns you expect for the MVP?
2) Any specific SLA thresholds for TTFT or p95 streaming that will be deal-breakers?

I'll kick off the tests on Monday and loop you in as soon as initial CSVs are ready.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
(alex.martinez@redwood.ai)

---
Attachment: medsys_map_v1.pdf (MAP draft, 3 pages)
From: Suresh Patel <suresh@medsys.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@medsys.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan + TTFT streaming benchmark — proposed timeline

Alex —

Thanks for the clear plan and fast turnaround. The proposed timeline looks fine from our side — Nov 25 for initial results is good. A few clarifications:

- Concurrency: 1/8/32 is fine, but can you also include an intermediate 16-run case if it's low marginal cost? We expect some sustained bursts in the 12–18 thread range.
- Metrics: For p99 TTFT we need to understand tail behavior under a 5-minute spike test (simulated burst). Please include a short-run spike test in addition to steady-state.
- Security: Our security team will likely ask for the test harness and any credentials used during the canary. We'll need a brief runbook that explains audit/log collection during the canary.

Also, please send the raw CSVs and summary tables as soon as available so our infra folks can start a quick review.

Thanks —
Suresh
VP Product | MedSys
(suresh@medsys.com)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Suresh Patel <suresh@medsys.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan + TTFT streaming benchmark — initial results attached

Suresh / team —

Attached are the initial bench artifacts (ttft_stream_results.csv) and a two-page summary. Quick executive summary from our run (rwd-vicuna-13b-q4 on Dedicated pool, warmed KV cache after 5 minutes):

Test conditions:
- Prompts: short (32 tokens), medium (128 tokens), long (512 tokens)
- Concurrency targets: 1, 8, 16, 32
- Spike test: 5-minute ramp to 50 concurrent sessions (simulated) then steady-state back to target concurrency
- Network: us-west region, 10 ms average network hop to customer ingress in our lab

Key results (TTFT = time from request ingress to first token emitted):
- Short prompts (32 tokens):
  - concurrency 1: TTFT p50=85ms, p95=240ms, p99=510ms
  - concurrency 8: TTFT p50=120ms, p95=420ms, p99=890ms
  - concurrency 16: TTFT p50=150ms, p95=520ms, p99=1.1s
  - concurrency 32: TTFT p50=260ms, p95=1.1s, p99=2.6s

- Medium prompts (128 tokens):
  - concurrency 1: TTFT p50=110ms, p95=310ms, p99=650ms
  - concurrency 8: TTFT p50=160ms, p95=560ms, p99=1.2s
  - concurrency 16: TTFT p50=220ms, p95=830ms, p99=1.8s
  - concurrency 32: TTFT p50=420ms, p95=1.6s, p99=3.4s

Streaming per-token latencies (steady-state, medium prompt):
- concurrency 1: p50=12ms/token, p95=42ms/token, p99=110ms/token
- concurrency 8: p50=18ms/token, p95=78ms/token, p99=210ms/token
- concurrency 16: p50=25ms/token, p95=120ms/token, p99=380ms/token
- concurrency 32: p50=44ms/token, p95=250ms/token, p99=720ms/token

Spike test notes: during the 5-minute burst to 50 concurrent sessions we saw TTFT p99 climbing to ~4.2s for short prompts; error rate remained <0.2% (mostly transient 503s that cleared with retry backoff).

Attachments: ttft_stream_results.csv contains the raw sample-level timing. medsys_canary_playbook.docx is a draft runbook with audit/log hooks and required credentials handling notes.

Next steps I recommend:
- We add the 16-concurrency column (done) and include the 5-minute spike numbers in the summary (included).
- Joint review on Nov 29 to decide canary window and SLA guardrails (p95 streaming <800ms and p99 TTFT <2s for medium prompts is our suggestion for canary pass).

Let me know if you want us to re-run with a cold-cache baseline or change prompt mixes — we can schedule that overnight.

-Marissa
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
(marissa.cole@redwood.ai)

Attachments: ttft_stream_results.csv (CSV, ~1.4MB), medsys_canary_playbook.docx (DOCX, 6 pages)

To: Suresh Patel <suresh@medsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan + TTFT streaming benchmark — initial results attached

Suresh / Priya —

Thanks — this is great and aligns with our expectations. A few points and proposed actions so we can finalize the MAP: 

- Canary pass criteria (proposal):
  - Medium prompts: streaming p95 < 800ms AND TTFT p99 < 2s during a 24-hour canary at expected traffic mix.
  - Error rate < 0.5% for 5xx during canary window.
  - Spike behavior: 5-minute 50-concurrency spike should not push p99 TTFT > 5s (we observed ~4.2s in the run).

- Next steps:
  1) Alex to send DocuSign for the MAP addendum by Mon Nov 29 (link: https://www.docusign.com/Signing/?s=MS-2026-042).
  2) Marissa to own canary support and logs collection; Rafael will be oncall for infra during Dec 7–9 canary.
  3) MedSys to confirm any additional data retention/compliance asks prior to canary.

If that all looks good I'll route the MAP addendum for signature and schedule the Nov 29 review meeting (30 minutes) to lock the canary window.

Appreciate the fast alignment — excited to get this into a canary.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
(alex.martinez@redwood.ai)
